title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: data data.frame least one text column containing raw responses. Additional columns (e.g., grouping variables) preserved pipeline. Coding stages: "preprocess", "valence", "dictionaries", "socats", "embeddings", "seeds", "aggregate".
code: dat <- data.frame(   responsex = c("warm and friendly", "cold and rde", "smart worker", NA),   Target = c("A", "A", "B", "B"),   Participant = c("1", "2", "3", "4"),   stringsAsFactors = FALSE )

title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: Cleans normalizes text responses. Produces three text columns: tv: lowercased text (used valence scoring) tv2: spell-checked text tv3: singularized text (used dictionary matching) Two spell-checking methods available via spellcheck_method parameter: "hunspell" (default): Uses Java + WordNet + hunspell. Suggestions ranked edit distance, bigram context tiebreaker corpus 50+ unique values. Auto-detects Java WordNet paths across macOS/Linux/Windows. auto-detection fails, set explicit java_home / wordnet_dict arguments environment variables (JAVA_HOME, SADCAT_WORDNET_DICT). "gemini": RECOMMENDED SPELL-CHECKING METHOD. Uses Gemini LLM context-aware correction. Sends full responses (individual words) model can use surrounding context. Requires Gemini API key via gemini_spellcheck_key GEMINI_API_KEY environment variable. May require updating model, check: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models. can also provide custom context prompt via gemini_spellcheck_context give model information domain text data. default prompt describes text short responses describing social target.
code: dat <- preprocess_text(   dat,   text_col = "responsex",   spellcheck = TRUE,                     # TRUE enables spell-checking   spellcheck_method = "gemini",         # "hunspell" (default) or "gemini"   singularize = TRUE,   java_home = NULL,                       # optional; used for hunspell only   wordnet_dict = NULL,                    # optional; used for hunspell only   gemini_spellcheck_key = NULL,           # optional; used for gemini only   gemini_spellcheck_model = "gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview",   gemini_spellcheck_context = NULL,       # optional custom Gemini prompt   verbose = TRUE )  # Inspect: what did preprocessing change? dat[, c("responsex", "tv", "tv2", "tv3")]

title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: Scores response 5 sentiment dictionaries (Lexicoder/LSD2015, NRC, Bing, AFINN, Loughran). Produces per-dictionary scores combined scores negation handling. Key output columns: ValenceYesNA: Combined valence. Mean negation-aware scores across 5 dictionaries. NA dictionary matched sentiment words. Negation applied combined score. ValenceNoNA: ValenceYesNA, 0 instead NA.
code: dat <- score_valence(   dat,   text_col = "tv2",             # recommend using "tv2" for human participants   response_col = "responsex"    # NA-gating column; NULL defaults to text_col )  # Inspect valence dat[, c("responsex", "Val_lexicoder", "Val_NRC", "Val_bing", "Val_affin", "Val_loughran", "ValenceYesNA", "ValenceNoNA")]

title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: Matches text SADCAT stereotype content dictionaries computes binary indicators, percentages, direction scores, per-dimension valence. Key output columns (per dimension, e.g., Warmth, Competence, Morality, …): {Dim}_prevalence: 1 match, 0 none, NA response missing {Dim}_Valence (default downstream means): NA dimension absent; otherwise global ValenceNoNA (0 sentiment-less tagged responses, signed value otherwise). Use mean(., na.rm = TRUE) average tagged responses sentiment-less ones contribute 0 (neutral). {Dim}_valenceStrictNA: NA dimension absent ValenceYesNA NA. Strictly NA-gated axes. {Dim}_valenceNoNA: 0 dimension absent sentiment matched; NA response missing. {Dim}_direction (directional dimensions ): hi-lo direction, NA applicable {Dim}_directionNoNA (directional dimensions ): {Dim}_direction, 0 dimension absent (still NA response missing) NoMatch: 1 SADCAT dimension matched (NA response missing) Note: Warmth = Sociability + Morality; Competence = Ability + Assertiveness. Beauty subdimension Appearance. Words may fall multiple dictionaries.
code: dat <- match_dictionaries(   dat,   text_col = "tv3",   response_col = "responsex",   # NA-gating column; NULL defaults to text_col   valence_col = "ValenceYesNA",   valence_nona_col = "ValenceNoNA",   sadcat_dict = NULL,           # NULL auto-loads SADCAT dictionaries   socats_dict = NULL,           # NULL auto-loads SOCATS only if socats = TRUE   socats = TRUE                 # include Social categories dictionaries as well (optional; default FALSE) )  # Inspect dimension-level results View(dat)  #Inspect top 20 words matching each dimension (for sanity check and to understand what the dictionaries are capturing) get_top_dictionary_matches(dat, text_col = "tv3", top_n = 20)

title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: Generates sentence embeddings via SBERT /Gemini. Requires Python via reticulate.
code: dat <- compute_embeddings(   dat,   text_col = "tv",   response_col = "responsex",   # NA-gating column; NULL defaults to text_col   methods = c("sbert", "gemini"),           # or "sbert" if gemini not set up   sbert_model = "paraphrase-mpnet-base-v2",   sbert_dims = 768L,   gemini_api_key = NULL,       # required only when methods includes "gemini" and key not set via env var   gemini_model = "gemini-embedding-001",   gemini_dims = 768L,   gemini_batch_size = 10L,   gemini_sleep = 63,   gemini_task_type = "SEMANTIC_SIMILARITY",   verbose = TRUE )

title: Pipeline Usage Guide
text: Computes correlation (cosine similarity) response embeddings SADCAT seed vectors. Requires embeddings Stage 4.
code: dat <- compute_seed_similarities(   dat,   embedding_prefix = c("SBERT", "Gemini"),  # or only one model, based on stage 4 decisions   seed_vectors = Seed_Vectors_Avg,   method = "correlation",      # or "cosine"   response_col = "responsex",  # NA-gating column   verbose = TRUE )

title: Run the Full SADCAT Pipeline — process_responses
text: Stage--stage usage. stage can called standalone exported function. useful inspecting intermediate results, customizing parameters per stage, integrating external processing. functions must called order stage depends columns produced earlier stages: Valence columns. ValenceYesNA: Mean negation-aware scores across 5 sentiment     dictionaries. NA dictionary matched sentiment word. Negation     applied combined score, individual dictionary scores. ValenceNoNA: ValenceYesNA, 0 instead NA. Val_lexicoder, Val_NRC, etc.: Per-dictionary raw     presence scores (-1, 0, 1) without negation flipping. {Dim}_prevalence: 1/0 dimension prevalence, NA response     missing. {Dim}_Valence: Default per-dimension valence. NA     dimension tagged; otherwise ValenceNoNA (0 sentiment-less     tagged responses, signed value otherwise). Best mean(., na.rm=TRUE). {Dim}_valenceStrictNA: NA dimension tagged     ValenceYesNA NA. Strictly NA-gated axes. {Dim}_valenceNoNA: 0 dimension tagged     sentiment matched; NA response missing. {Dim}_direction: Direction score directional dimensions     (NA applicable). {Dim}_directionNoNA: {Dim}_direction, 0     dimension absent (NA response missing). NoMatch: 1 SADCAT dimension matched, 0 otherwise     (NA response missing).
code: # Stage 1: Preprocess -> produces tv, tv2, tv3 dat <- preprocess_text(dat, text_col = "responsex", spellcheck = FALSE)  # Stage 2: Valence -> produces Val_*, ValenceYesNA, ValenceNoNA dat <- score_valence(dat, text_col = "tv")  # Stage 3: SADCAT dictionaries -> produces compact outputs such as # {Dim}_prevalence, {Dim}_Valence, {Dim}_valenceStrictNA, {Dim}_valenceNoNA, # {Dim}_direction, and NoMatch dat <- match_dictionaries(dat, text_col = "tv3",                           valence_col = "ValenceYesNA", valence_nona_col = "ValenceNoNA")  # Stage 3b (optional): SOCATS social category dictionaries dat <- match_dictionaries(dat, text_col = "tv3",                           valence_col = "ValenceYesNA", valence_nona_col = "ValenceNoNA",                           sadcat_dict = FALSE, socats = TRUE)  # Stage 4 (optional): Sentence embeddings (requires Python via reticulate) dat <- compute_embeddings(dat, text_col = "tv", methods = "sbert")  # Stage 5 (optional): Seed similarities (requires Stage 4) dat <- compute_seed_similarities(dat, embedding_prefix = "SBERT")  # Stage 6: Aggregate to group level agg <- aggregate_responses(dat,           group_cols = c("Synonym.GroupX", "Group", "Level"))

title: SADCAT 2.0.0
text: Direction columns now contain -1, 0, +1, NA. Two corrupted “2” codings repaired (“accepting” +1 Morality Warmth; censorial/censoring/censorship family -1 ), along corrupted SentiWordNet/AFINN valence cells. Membership direction now consistent everywhere: word direction member directional dimension. 97 Politics/Religion membership flags added manually added words carried directions; roughly 150 member words missing directions manually coded; stray directions non-member words removed. _dict_hi / _dict_lo columns rebuilt membership plus direction (+1 / -1). 1,400 word-dimension pairs manually added vocabulary now contribute pipeline direction scoring, direction scores shift relative earlier versions. Val recomputed component columns; _dict_Pos / _dict_Neg recomputed membership crossed sign Val. 38 duplicated .steps_Dictionaries rows merged; value columns cleaned (stray strings, trailing spaces, TRUE/FALSE casing, values2/values3 normalized documented recipe). Dimension hierarchy enforced: Sociability Morality membership implies Warmth membership; Ability Assertiveness membership implies Competence membership. Removed legacy columns Beliefs_dict_ABC*, work_dir_dummy, beliefsother_dir_dummy datasets. Dictionaries Dictionaries_FT longer shipped package data. Dictionaries stale relative .steps_Dictionaries (lacked 1,100 stems, including manually added vocabulary). files remain available unchanged archived-data/ GitHub. Removed Code_words() Code_single(), legacy word-coding API built archived Dictionaries data. Use current pipeline (preprocess_text(), score_valence(), match_dictionaries()) instead. Full_preprocess() now uses .steps_Dictionaries$values3 spellcheck wordlist. Documentation updated actual column set .steps_Dictionaries (tv, values, values2, values3). Please cite data-corrected release SADCAT 2.0.0.

title: SADCAT 0.2.0 (development)
text: score_valence() adds three new dictionaries default: SentiWordNet, Warriner et al. (2013) affective norms, Jockers/Rinker lexicon now applied alongside existing five (Lexicoder, NRC, Bing, AFINN, Loughran), bringing combined ValenceYesNA / ValenceNoNA averages 8 dictionaries. New parameters: include_sentiwn (default TRUE), sentiwn_threshold (default 0.10) use SentiWordNet column already bundled Sentiments$Val_sentiwn, presence-based scoring -1 / 0 / +1. threshold filters marginal-magnitude entries (default 0.10 keeps 32k 38k). include_warriner (default TRUE) uses Warriner et al. (2013) norms bundled new Warriner_norms dataset (13,905 lemmas; original 1-9 Likert linearly rescaled [-1, 1] via (V.Mean.Sum - 5) / 4). Continuous-valued: text’s Val_warriner mean matched-word valences. Validated common English vocabulary; widely used person-perception, social cognition, prejudice research. include_jockers (default TRUE) uses Jockers/Rinker lexicon bundled new Jockers_norms dataset (11,697 entries; continuous valence [-1, 1]). 13 entries upstream lexicon source fell outside [-1, 1] (e.g., overly = -2, = -1.05, much = -2) dropped shifter / amplifier coefficients designed sentimentr’s sliding-window aggregator, independently sentiment-bearing words. Validation context narrative/literary text rather person perception specifically; use caveat. Negation handling preserved: positive Warriner/Jockers word inside negation scope contributes negated value combined average. Set include_* FALSE opt individual dictionary; set three FALSE recover prior 5-dictionary output exactly. Behavior change vs. 0.1.0: existing callers score_valence() see ValenceYesNA / ValenceNoNA shift, additional Val_* columns, increased coverage previously--match responses (≈22% rescue default thresholds 47.8k-row human-response corpus).

title: SADCAT 0.2.0 (development)
text: singularize2() now actually singularizes -es plurals: stray (stringr::str_detect(word, "es$")) return(word) early-return made irregular-plural switch (valves → valve, ladies → lady, boxes → box, etc.) ves/ies/zes/ses/es suffix block dead code. Removed early-return branches run intended; also reordered opening guards .na(word) checked dictionary membership. behavior fix (correctness): words ending -es previously returned unchanged now singularized. singularize2() -zes / -ses branch longer -strips: branch previously stripped three trailing characters unconditionally, freezes → free, noses → , roses → ro, etc. (results happened valid dictionary entries completely different meanings silently accepted). now tries candidate suffixes order: strip s (freezes → freeze, noses → nose, houses → house), strip es (buses → bus, gases → gas, classes → class), strip zes/ses (quizzes → quiz), keeping first ’s SemNetDictionaries::general.dictionary. Known remaining edge case: Latin -plurals like crises still mis-singularize general.dictionary contains spurious short fragments (e.g., cris) beat crisis; fixing requires dictionary cleanup, logic changes. singularize2() longer mangles short inputs singular -ss nouns: three guards added. Words shorter 3 characters short-circuit return unchanged ("" longer becomes "", "" longer becomes "us", "" longer becomes "", "" longer becomes ""). final -s stripping branch now skips words ending -ss, preventing mass → mas pass → pas. stripping rule, candidate shorter 3 characters falls back original word, preventing bus → bu axes → ax. Spellcheck2() longer mangles NA markers: previously, hunspell receive inputs like "n/" "?" offer nonsense suggestions ("n/" → "naan", "?" → "s"), propagated pipeline got aggregated content responses instead missing data. Spellcheck2() now short-circuits hunspell input letters digits (pure punctuation: "?", "--", "...") matches explicit n/variant ("n/", "N/", "n..", "#N/", etc.) returns canonical "na" placeholder.

title: SADCAT 0.2.0 (development)
text: Global valence rename: score_valence() now outputs ValenceYesNA instead Valence. ValenceNoNA unchanged. Downstream code reads data$Valence must migrate data$ValenceYesNA. Per-dimension valence columns renamed extended: match_dictionaries() now produces three per-dimension valence columns instead two. column formerly named {Dim}_valence now {Dim}_valenceStrictNA; new default column {Dim}_Valence (capital V): common substitution _valence → _Valence (capital V), silently changes semantics downstream means: tagged responses matched sentiment words now contribute 0 (neutral) rather dropped NA. Verify desired behaviour migrating. match_dictionaries() default parameter: valence_col default changed "Valence" "ValenceYesNA" match renamed output score_valence(). Callers pass old default explicitly must update.
